articles.title: ITBP’s New Strategy: Drones, Shaurya Commandos & Bunkers to Counter China’s LAC Challenge
articles.description: Drones above the mountains, specialised commandos on the ground and underground shelters along the frontier. The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) is upgrading its preparations along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China. In this Defence HQ explainer, we examine the force’s expanding drone capabilities, the role of its Shaurya commando platoons and plans to develop underground shelters at forward posts.ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor has outlined a ₹400-crore allocation, with 70% earmarked for strengthening drone warfare capabilities. Separately, the Home Ministry has given in-principle approval to a ₹4,000-crore modernisation scheme that includes a proposed ₹1,000 crore for drone and anti-drone systems. The force is also raising Shaurya commando platoons, training personnel for high-altitude contingencies and developing better-protected infrastructure for troops deployed in extreme Himalayan conditions.
